title: Historical timeseries gap-filler with resumable checkpointing
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: We discovered gaps and late-arriving records in the usage timeseries that feed the Console cost and latency dashboards. These gaps occur when downstream transform jobs skip windows after transient store timeouts or when re-ingest of partial blobs fails. Goal: deliver a safe, resumable gap-filler tool that can compute a compact work plan, run a dry-run diff, and then perform idempotent upserts to the canonical events table without double-counting or breaking derived aggregates. The tool must support partitioned execution, checkpoint tokens, and cost estimates for large ranges. It should be usable by SREs and analytics owners via Airflow DAG and a CLI for one-off runs.
acceptance_criteria: Tool produces a compact plan of affected partitions for a user-specified time range
Dry-run mode computes delta counts and shows potential duplicate keys without mutating tables
Resumable checkpoint tokens allow cancelling and resuming mid-run with exactly-once semantics
Idempotent writes to BigQuery/Events store ensure aggregator dashboards do not change outside of expected deltas
End-to-end runbooks and an Airflow DAG are checked in and documented in Confluence
tasks: Design compact partition plan: time-window + source-seqno ranges
Prototype dry-run comparator that samples affected keys and estimates token costs
Implement resumable worker with checkpoint token persisted to S3 and Redis lease
Add idempotent upsert layer using canonical event fingerprint and partial update strategy
Integrate with Airflow as a parametrized DAG (start, end, dry-run, concurrency)
Add tracing hooks to Console observability (trace-id per run) and Grafana dashboard
Create runbook and playbook for manual invocations and emergency rollback

implementation_notes: Run architecture: controller creates immutable plan and shards into workers keyed by partition; workers claim a shard via Redis lease and persist checkpoint to S3 after each completed shard segment.

Idempotency: use deterministic event fingerprint (sha256 of canonicalized payload fields) and upsert semantics in BigQuery with MERGE by fingerprint + timestamp, avoid full table scans by writing to staging table per shard then merge.
Throttling: adaptive token-bucket per-worker to avoid saturating KV cache and downstream ingestion; default concurrency 4 per node, tunable by runtime flag
Cost control: tool emits cost estimate in dry-run (estimated token + egress) and will require explicit --force to run if estimate > $2000 for interactive runs
Observability: emit structured run events to ops-events stream with trace_id, shard_id, processed_count, error_count, last_checkpoint_ts
rollback_plan: If dashboards show regressions, run a reverse-merge using previous snapshot for affected partitions (snapshot created at start of each run) and revert staging merges. Emergency toggle: set DAG to dry-run-only and run compensating merges. Documented in runbook.
notes: Design decision: prefer small, resumable shards instead of huge one-shot backfills to reduce blast radius. We will later generalize the controller to support reprocessing other event types.
